quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should:

options.text: Spread out to make the group easier to see.
Stay close together to make the group easier to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together to make the group easier to see.
questions.explanation: Staying close together makes the group easier for other drivers to see. It also keeps riders from getting separated. Riders should leave space to move safely, but not pair up.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Squeeze both brakes smoothly and firmly. Use more front brake as the weight shifts forward. Keep your knees against the tank and eyes up to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do one action first, then the other. Do not brake and swerve at the same time, as this can make your motorcycle tip over.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Alternate between your headlight's low and high beam settings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam in rain or fog. High beams reflect off water and fog, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that are parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle.
Avoid crossing the tracks for any reason.
Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to cross the tracks at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross parallel tracks at a 45-degree angle with a quick, sharp turn. Do not inch across slowly—the tracks could catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing even with a helmet. Wear ear protection. It will still let you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, which riding formation should be used?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best for straight roads.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge your location and speed.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden moves. Stay away from the center lane and follow tire tracks left by cars.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually safest to approach the tracks:

options.text: By proceeding straight within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: By proceeding straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight ahead in your lane when crossing angled tracks. Turning to hit them at a right angle could push you into another lane.

questions.question: How should you pack a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavier items toward the front of the load. Loads should sit over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: When your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, what can you do?

options.text: Use less pressure on the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight moves forward while braking, the front wheel gets more traction. This means you can apply the front brake harder.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders be placed in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Place inexperienced riders just behind the lead rider. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: To prevent collisions at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a close group?

options.text: It takes up less space on the highway.
The group is easier to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders reach their destination faster in a close group than a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a close group is better because it uses less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights or during passes. Speed does not increase.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. But they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: Signals help riders in groups communicate. When the lead rider extends their right leg, it warns of a hazard on the right side of the road.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It discourages the passing driver from cutting in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
It encourages the passing driver to complete the pass quickly.
It encourages other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It encourages the passing driver to cut in too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane when being passed is dangerous. It may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this area safe for motorcyclists?

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of traffic lanes. When the road is dry, this area usually has enough grip for motorcycles. When wet, avoid it. The oily strip is narrow, so you can usually ride to one side and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about hazards ahead.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting gears harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes with road and traffic conditions. Move your position to stay safe and make sure other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use brakes, but downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently when you need to slow down or stop.
